scope: Original performance language references for Marion & Lucas / MonIA
source_policy: Use uploaded drama excerpts only to extract broad performance, pacing, framing, gaze, blocking, tension and wardrobe-context traits. Do not reproduce copyrighted footage, dialogue, actor identity, exact likeness, exact voice, or shot-for-shot staging.

presence: attraction comes from restraint rather than overt performance
micro-expressions matter more than large gestures
brief half-smiles, small eyebrow shifts, slight jaw tension, subtle breath changes
eye contact can be intense but should break naturally rather than stay fixed
gaze: short downward or side glances before returning to the other person
listening should remain visibly active: blinking, breathing, tiny focus shifts
reaction often begins in the eyes before the mouth
pacing: allow silences and beats before answers
avoid constant motion or constant smiling
emotional tension should build through pauses, proximity and withholding
speech turns should feel measured, not presenter-like
body_language: leaning slightly closer only when context warrants it
subtle changes in distance can carry intimacy or tension
wardrobe_context: formal tailoring can signal public/social settings
open-collar white or dark shirts can signal private or late-evening contexts
wardrobe must vary with story context; no permanent black-shirt uniform

intimacy: close framing can work when motivated by the scene, but avoid permanent extreme close-up
use proximity, gaze breaks, pauses and body positioning before overt gestures
keep interactions original to Marion & Lucas and context-driven
camera: favor human, imperfect framing over polished advertising composition
for visio specifically, use believable front-camera grammar rather than cinematic coverage
micro-movements and slight framing drift help sell liveness
lighting: warm practical light can support intimate/private moments
higher-contrast evening lighting can add tension without becoming stylized or artificial

always_alive: Lucas must remain visually alive while listening: blinking, breathing, tiny gaze shifts, posture adjustments
do not freeze on a single frame while the player chooses a response
listening, reacting, speaking and transition states must blend without obvious hard cuts
speaking: spoken reply must correspond to the visible mouth performance
never overlay unrelated audio on a looping speaking clip
preserve validated Lucas identity, eyes and current approved voice baseline
interaction: player choices may drive intent, but Lucas should react visually before and during his spoken response
the result should feel like a person present on the other end of a live call, not a visual novel overlay
